messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: mdply bug?
parts:
Dear list,

Consider the following example,

library(plyr)

foo <- function(a="a", b="b", c="c", ...){
paste(a, b, c, sep="")
}

mdply(data.frame(b=1:4), foo)
b V1
1 1 1bc
2 2 2bc
3 3 3bc
4 4 4bc

It seems to me that the result is incorrect, the input variable "b"
has been interpreted as "a". If the input data.frame contains more
than one variable it works,

mdply(data.frame(b=1:4, c="c"), foo)
b c V1
1 1 c a1c
2 2 c a2c
3 3 c a3c
4 4 c a4c


Looks like a bug to me.

Best regards,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: mdply bug?
parts:
... and looking at the source the problem seems to be in splitter_a(),

splitter_a(data.frame(b=1:4), 1)
# unnamed object, hence the result is passed as first argument

splitter_a(data.frame(b=1:4, c="c"), 1)
# named lists, OK

The problem is probably coming from here:

indexed_array(environment(), indices)

but I don't really understand what this function does.

Best,

baptiste

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: mdply bug?
parts:
> splitter_a(data.frame(b=1:4), 1)
> # unnamed object, hence the result is passed as first argument
>
> splitter_a(data.frame(b=1:4, c="c"), 1)
> # named lists, OK
>
> The problem is probably coming from here:
>
> indexed_array(environment(), indices)

It's basically an efficient version of split adapted to arrays that
tries to avoid copying the data (and thus has to use environments)

The problem comes from "[[.indexed_array" which currently uses drop =
TRUE when subsetting the array. I've now switched to using drop =
FALSE when the data is an data frame, and TRUE otherwise. The bug is
fixed on github.

Hadley

PS. In future, it would be very helpful if you could contribute bug
reports in the form of test cases. I've written a new package for
testing called testthat (docs attached) and any comments would be
appreciated.

--
